Q: When or why should I use numpy.meshgrid (Ny,Nx) arrays instead of two (1,Nx) and (Ny,1) arrays? A:

When to use np.meshgrid

You should usually use np.meshgrid when using coordinates, since it is better for plotting, and easier to index. This is because when you use np.meshgrid each coordinate in a plot is represented as (x[i, j], y[i, j], z[i, j]). When you do not use np.meshgrid it is not immediately clear whether a coordinate is represented as (x[i], y[j], z[i, j]) or (x[i], y[j], z[j, i]). This is why plotting libraries like matplotlib expect xx, yy and zz as arguments for 3D plots.

When to not use np.meshgrid

You should use tricks like in your example when making expansive calculations where you make use of different array sizes and eg. sum over different axes at different points. I would however suggest using np.newaxis instead of np.reshape to make your code more readable. This makes it clear which axis belongs to the x data and which belongs to the y data in your final result. This would look like this:

x = np.array([1,2,3,4,5])[np.newaxis, :]
y = np.array([6,7,8])[:, np.newaxis]

For more complex examples this makes it much easier to see whether it compiles and what happens. In this meaningless example:

x = np.array([1,2,3,4,5])
y = np.array([6,7,8])

np.sum(x[:, np.newaxis]*y[np.newaxis, :], axis=1)[:, np.newaxis]+np.sum(x[:, np.newaxis]*y[np.newaxis, :], axis=0)[np.newaxis, :]

It is pretty doable to deduce that the final shape will be (Nx, Ny), while this would be much harder when using np.reshape.

Performance speed

For performance speed it doesn't really matter. If there is a lot of calculations done on x and y separately, it is slower with np.meshgrid, but when there is a lot of calculations combining x and y, it is faster with np.meshgrid. For example, in your example the first option is faster, but when you do not square x and y first, then meshgrid is faster.

Q: Handler dispatch failed; nested exception is java.lang.NoSuchMethodError A:

You should upgrade the runtime environment. In your current runtime version of Java EE javax.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest does not contain a method with the name getHttpServletMapping. Java EE 8 Introduce the method getHttpServletMapping.Or make sure that you are using the same version for development and runtime. References: JAVA EE github docsApache Tomcat docs

Q: Fixing PHP PEAR error A:

You said that

It is PHP's default setting for include_path is ".;/path/to/php/pear" which is what the answer suggested.

You need to change that to the actual path to pear on your install. I use XAMPP under windows and have not trouble with this because I changed mine to .;\xampp\php\PEAR because that is where xampp default puts the installation of PEAR.

I also had to change a few things. See my answer in the Getting PEAR to work on XAMPP (Apache/MySQL stack on Windows) question for details on the pear config changes I had to make.
